authors.Emily Dickinson: Emily Dickinson (1830–1886) was an American poet whose compressed, formally inventive lyrics explore nature, love, mortality, faith, and the inner life.
authors.William Shakespeare: William Shakespeare (1564–1616) was an English playwright and poet whose plays and poems have had an enduring influence on world literature and theatre.
authors.Percy Bysshe Shelley: Percy Bysshe Shelley (1792–1822) was an English Romantic poet whose lyric and dramatic writing joined radical political hope with an intense attention to nature and the imagination.
authors.Walt Whitman: Walt Whitman (1819–1892) was an American poet whose expansive free verse celebrated the self, democracy, and nature.
authors.Ralph Waldo Emerson: Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882) was an American essayist, lecturer, and poet central to Transcendentalism.
authors.Li Bai (李白): Li Bai (701–762) was a major Tang-dynasty Chinese poet whose vivid landscapes, friendship poems, soaring imagination, and independent voice made him one of the central figures of classical Chinese literature.
authors.Matsuo Bashō (松尾芭蕉): Matsuo Bashō (1644–1694) was a Japanese poet who brought haiku to lasting artistic prominence.
authors.Alexander Pushkin: Alexander Pushkin (1799–1837) was a Russian poet, playwright, and novelist whose verse and prose were foundational to modern Russian literature.
authors.Rainer Maria Rilke: Rainer Maria Rilke (1875–1926) was a Bohemian-Austrian poet and prose writer whose German-language work examines perception, solitude, transformation, art, and spiritual life.
authors.Heinrich Heine: Heinrich Heine (1797–1856) was a German poet, essayist, and journalist known for the lyric clarity, musicality, irony, and political intelligence of his writing.
authors.Rabindranath Tagore: Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a Bengali poet, essayist, composer, and educator who reshaped modern Indian literature. He received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature and prepared the English texts used here himself.
authors.Misuzu Kaneko: Misuzu Kaneko (1903–1930) was a Japanese poet of children's verse whose poems attend closely to overlooked lives, natural things, empathy, and difference. About ninety of her poems appeared in magazines during her lifetime.
authors.Fernando Pessoa: Fernando Pessoa (1888–1935) was a Portuguese poet and prose writer who created distinct literary personae, including Álvaro de Campos, Alberto Caeiro, and Ricardo Reis, to explore identity, perception, modernity, and consciousness.
authors.Fyodor Dostoevsky: Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821–1881) was a Russian novelist and short-story writer known for psychologically searching works about conscience, freedom, suffering, and moral responsibility.
authors.Friedrich Nietzsche: Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900) was a German philosopher, cultural critic, philologist, and writer whose aphoristic works examine value, knowledge, self-creation, art, and the affirmation of life.
authors.Edith Södergran: Edith Södergran (1892–1923) was a Finland-Swedish modernist poet whose compressed, visionary work explores identity, freedom, love, nature, and the inner life.
authors.Charles Baudelaire: Charles Baudelaire (1821–1867) was a French poet, critic, and translator whose formally exacting work transformed the modern lyric through its attention to beauty, urban life, memory, and the divided self.
authors.Edward Thomas: Edward Thomas (1878–1917) was an Anglo-Welsh poet and prose writer whose closely observed landscapes join everyday speech, memory, uncertainty, and the pressures of historical change.
authors.Anton Chekhov: Anton Chekhov (1860–1904) was a Russian physician, short-story writer, and dramatist whose formally subtle fiction and plays examine ordinary lives, moral attention, change, and the distance between aspiration and action.
authors.Virginia Woolf: Virginia Woolf (1882–1941) was an English novelist, essayist, and publisher whose modernist writing explores consciousness, time, memory, artistic form, and women’s intellectual freedom.
authors.Kahlil Gibran: Kahlil Gibran (1883–1931) was a Lebanese-born writer and visual artist who wrote in Arabic and English; his poetry, parables, essays, and fiction explore love, freedom, spiritual life, exile, and human fellowship.
authors.Federico García Lorca: Federico García Lorca (1898–1936) was a Spanish poet and dramatist whose lyrical, symbol-rich work explores love, solitude, nature, identity, and human dignity.
authors.Henry Wadsworth Longfellow: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1807–1882) was an American poet and educator whose accessible, musical verse reflects on perseverance, memory, nature, and shared humanity.
authors.César Vallejo: César Vallejo (1892–1938) was a Peruvian poet whose formally inventive work joins compassion, spiritual questioning, family memory, and the pressures of modern life.
authors.Rubén Darío: Rubén Darío (1867–1916) was a Nicaraguan poet and a central figure of Spanish-language modernismo, known for musical form, vivid imagery, and a searching engagement with beauty, time, and hope.
authors.Marina Tsvetaeva: Marina Tsvetaeva (1892–1941) was a Russian poet whose compressed rhythms and daring voice explore imagination, memory, freedom, intimacy, and the inner resources of language.
authors.Giosuè Carducci: Giosuè Carducci (1835–1907) was an Italian poet, critic, and classical scholar whose formally disciplined verse joins landscape, civic memory, love, grief, and the passage of time.
authors.Kobayashi Issa: Kobayashi Issa (1763–1828) was a Japanese haiku poet whose plainspoken, compassionate verse finds dignity, humor, and fellowship among children, travelers, small creatures, and the changing seasons.
authors.Akiko Yosano: Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) was a Japanese poet, essayist, translator, and advocate for women's education whose work joins intimate self-expression with intellectual freedom, social criticism, love, and renewal.
authors.Li Qingzhao (李清照): Li Qingzhao (1084–c. 1155) was a Song-dynasty poet and essayist whose formally precise ci poetry joins wit, natural observation, love, displacement, memory, and an unusually direct account of grief.
authors.Su Shi (苏轼): Su Shi (1037–1101) was a Northern Song poet, essayist, calligrapher, and statesman whose writing combines intellectual range, humor, friendship, close observation of nature, and resilient responses to exile.
authors.Rumi: Rumi (1207–1273), formally Jalal al-Din Muhammad Rumi, was a Persian-language poet, Islamic scholar, and Sufi mystic whose lyric and narrative works became central to Persian literary and spiritual traditions.
authors.Olaudah Equiano: Olaudah Equiano (c. 1745–1797), also known as Gustavus Vassa, was a writer, sailor, merchant, and leading Black abolitionist in Britain whose 1789 autobiography became an influential account of enslavement and freedom.
authors.Yun Dong-ju: Yun Dong-ju (1917–1945) was a Korean lyric poet whose work reflects conscience, colonial oppression, freedom, and hope; his posthumous collection Sky, Wind, Stars, and Poem made him one of Korea’s most widely remembered modern poets.
authors.Sappho: Sappho (c. 630–c. 570 BCE) was an Archaic Greek lyric poet from Lesbos whose surviving songs and fragments are renowned for their musical language and direct treatment of love, desire, memory, and ritual.
authors.Horace: Horace (65–8 BCE), or Quintus Horatius Flaccus, was a Roman lyric poet and satirist whose Odes, Satires, Epistles, and Ars Poetica shaped later European ideas of poetic form and the examined life.
authors.Al-Ma'arri: Al-Ma'arri (973–1057) was a blind Arab poet, philosopher, and letter writer from Ma'arrat al-Nu'man whose intellectually independent works examine reason, ethics, suffering, and inherited belief.
authors.Nguyễn Du: Nguyễn Du (1765–1820) was a Vietnamese poet and scholar-official, best known for The Tale of Kiều, whose mastery of lục bát verse made the work a landmark of Vietnamese literature.
authors.Henry Lawson: Henry Lawson (1867–1922) was an Australian short-story writer, poet, and balladist whose spare, vernacular writing portrayed ordinary lives, hardship, and fellowship in colonial and rural Australia.

entries.passageOriginal:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: The poem’s opening imagines hope as a bird that stays within the soul.

passages.en:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
passages.zh-Hans:
希望是那有羽毛的东西
栖息在灵魂之中，
passages.zh-Hant:
希望是那有羽毛的東西
棲息在靈魂之中，
passages.ja:
希望とは羽根を持つもの
魂の中にとまっている—
passages.ko:
희망은 깃털 달린 것
영혼에 내려앉아 있는 것—
passages.es:
La esperanza es esa cosa con plumas
que se posa en el alma—
passages.fr:
L’espoir est cette chose emplumée
qui se perche dans l’âme—
passages.de:
Hoffnung ist das Wesen mit Federn
das sich in der Seele niederlässt—
passages.it:
La speranza è quella cosa piumata
che si posa nell’anima—
passages.pt:
A esperança é a coisa com penas
que pousa na alma—
passages.ru:
Надежда — это существо с перьями,
Что садится в душе—
passages.sv:
Hoppet är det bevingade ting
som slår sig ned i själen—
passages.ar:
الأمل ذلك الشيء ذو الريش
الذي يحطّ في الروح—
passages.hi:
आशा वह पंखों वाली चीज़ है
जो आत्मा में बसेरा करती है—
passages.bn:
আশা হলো পালকওয়ালা সেই বস্তু
যা আত্মায় বসে—
passages.id:
Harapan adalah sesuatu yang berbulu
yang hinggap di dalam jiwa—
passages.tr:
Umut tüylü bir şeydir
ruha tüneyen—
passages.vi:
Hy vọng là vật có lông vũ
đậu trong tâm hồn—
passages.th:
ความหวังคือสิ่งที่มีขนนก
ซึ่งเกาะอยู่ในดวงวิญญาณ—

entries.passageOriginal:
Success is counted sweetest
By those who ne'er succeed.
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: The opening distinguishes the outward fact of success from the intense knowledge of it held by those who lack it.

passages.en:
Success is counted sweetest
By those who ne'er succeed.
passages.zh-Hans:
成功被尝作最甜
是由那些从未成功的人。
passages.zh-Hant:
成功被嚐作最甜
是由那些從未成功的人。
passages.ja:
成功を最も甘いと知るのは
成功したことのない人。
passages.ko:
성공을 가장 달다고 여기는 이는
한 번도 성공하지 못한 사람이다.
passages.es:
El éxito sabe más dulce
a quienes nunca triunfan.
passages.fr:
Le succès paraît le plus doux
à ceux qui ne réussissent jamais.
passages.de:
Am süßesten gilt der Erfolg
denen, die nie Erfolg haben.
passages.it:
Il successo è più dolce
per chi non riesce mai.
passages.pt:
O sucesso parece mais doce
a quem nunca vence.
passages.ru:
Слаще всего успех считают
те, кто не побеждал.
passages.sv:
Framgång smakar allra sötast
för dem som aldrig lyckas.
passages.ar:
يبدو النجاح أشد حلاوة
لمن لم ينجحوا قط.
passages.hi:
सफलता सबसे मीठी लगती है
उन्हें जो कभी सफल नहीं हुए।
passages.bn:
সাফল্য সবচেয়ে মধুর মনে হয়
যারা কখনও সফল হয়নি তাদের কাছে।
passages.id:
Keberhasilan terasa paling manis
bagi mereka yang tak pernah berhasil.
passages.tr:
Başarı en tatlı gelir
hiç başaramamış olanlara.
passages.vi:
Thành công được thấy ngọt ngào nhất
bởi những người chưa từng thành công.
passages.th:
ความสำเร็จหวานที่สุด
สำหรับผู้ที่ไม่เคยสำเร็จ

entries.passageOriginal:
Our share of night to bear,
Our share of morning,
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: Our share of night to bear
entries.englishWorkTitle: Our share of night to bear
entries.englishContextNote: Night and morning are set beside one another as portions of experience that each person must receive and carry.

passages.en:
Our share of night to bear,
Our share of morning,
passages.zh-Hans:
承担属于我们的那份黑夜，
也承担属于我们的那份清晨，
passages.zh-Hant:
承擔屬於我們的那份黑夜，
也承擔屬於我們的那份清晨，
passages.ja:
私たちの分の夜を担い、
私たちの分の朝も担う、
passages.ko:
우리 몫의 밤을 견디고,
우리 몫의 아침도 맞이한다,
passages.es:
Soportar nuestra parte de noche,
y nuestra parte de mañana,
passages.fr:
Porter notre part de nuit,
notre part de matin,
passages.de:
Unseren Anteil Nacht zu tragen,
unseren Anteil Morgen,
passages.it:
Portare la nostra parte di notte,
la nostra parte di mattino,
passages.pt:
Levar nossa parte de noite,
nossa parte de manhã,
passages.ru:
Нести свою долю ночи,
свою долю утра,
passages.sv:
Att bära vår del av natten,
vår del av morgonen,
passages.ar:
أن نحمل نصيبنا من الليل،
ونصيبنا من الصباح،
passages.hi:
रात का अपना हिस्सा सहना,
सुबह का अपना हिस्सा भी,
passages.bn:
রাতের যে ভাগ আমাদের, তা বহন করা,
সকালের ভাগটিও,
passages.id:
Menanggung bagian malam kita,
dan bagian pagi kita,
passages.tr:
Geceden payımıza düşeni taşımak,
sabahtan payımıza düşeni de,
passages.vi:
Mang phần đêm thuộc về ta,
và phần bình minh của ta,
passages.th:
แบกรับส่วนแห่งราตรีของเรา
และส่วนแห่งรุ่งเช้าของเรา

entries.passageOriginal:
If I can stop one heart from breaking,
I shall not live in vain;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: If I can stop one heart from breaking
entries.englishWorkTitle: If I can stop one heart from breaking
entries.englishContextNote: The speaker locates a life’s value in the concrete act of easing another person’s suffering.

passages.en:
If I can stop one heart from breaking,
I shall not live in vain;
passages.zh-Hans:
如果我能阻止一颗心破碎，
我便没有白活；
passages.zh-Hant:
如果我能阻止一顆心破碎，
我便沒有白活；
passages.ja:
ひとつの心が砕けるのを止められるなら、
私の生は無駄ではない。
passages.ko:
한 사람의 마음이 무너지는 것을 막을 수 있다면,
내 삶은 헛되지 않으리라.
passages.es:
Si puedo impedir que un corazón se rompa,
no habré vivido en vano;
passages.fr:
Si je peux empêcher un cœur de se briser,
je n’aurai pas vécu en vain ;
passages.de:
Wenn ich ein Herz vorm Brechen bewahren kann,
dann lebe ich nicht vergebens;
passages.it:
Se posso impedire a un cuore di spezzarsi,
non avrò vissuto invano;
passages.pt:
Se eu puder impedir que um coração se parta,
não terei vivido em vão;
passages.ru:
Если я смогу уберечь одно сердце от разрыва,
я проживу не напрасно;
passages.sv:
Om jag kan hindra ett hjärta från att brista,
har jag inte levt förgäves;
passages.ar:
إن استطعت أن أمنع قلباً واحداً من الانكسار،
فلن أكون قد عشت عبثاً؛
passages.hi:
यदि मैं एक हृदय को टूटने से बचा सकूँ,
तो मेरा जीवन व्यर्थ नहीं होगा;
passages.bn:
যদি একটি হৃদয়কে ভাঙা থেকে বাঁচাতে পারি,
তবে আমার জীবন বৃথা নয়;
passages.id:
Jika aku dapat mencegah satu hati patah,
hidupku tak akan sia-sia;
passages.tr:
Bir kalbin kırılmasını önleyebilirsem,
boşuna yaşamış olmayacağım;
passages.vi:
Nếu tôi có thể ngăn một trái tim tan vỡ,
tôi sẽ không sống uổng phí;
passages.th:
หากฉันหยุดหัวใจหนึ่งดวงไม่ให้แตกสลายได้
ฉันก็ไม่ได้มีชีวิตอย่างสูญเปล่า

entries.passageOriginal:
A wounded deer leaps highest,
I've heard the hunter tell;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: The poem begins with the paradox that injury may produce a final, extraordinary display of strength.

passages.en:
A wounded deer leaps highest,
I've heard the hunter tell;
passages.zh-Hans:
受伤的鹿跃得最高，
我听猎人这样说；
passages.zh-Hant:
受傷的鹿躍得最高，
我聽獵人這樣說；
passages.ja:
傷ついた鹿がいちばん高く跳ぶと、
狩人から聞いた。
passages.ko:
상처 입은 사슴이 가장 높이 뛴다고,
사냥꾼에게서 들었다.
passages.es:
El ciervo herido salta más alto,
he oído decir al cazador;
passages.fr:
Le cerf blessé bondit le plus haut,
j’ai entendu le chasseur le dire ;
passages.de:
Ein verwundeter Hirsch springt am höchsten,
so hörte ich den Jäger sagen;
passages.it:
Il cervo ferito salta più in alto,
l’ho udito dire dal cacciatore;
passages.pt:
O cervo ferido salta mais alto,
ouvi o caçador dizer;
passages.ru:
Раненый олень прыгает выше всех,
слышала я от охотника;
passages.sv:
En sårad hjort hoppar högst,
har jag hört jägaren säga;
passages.ar:
الغزال الجريح يقفز أعلى،
هكذا سمعت الصياد يقول؛
passages.hi:
घायल हिरन सबसे ऊँचा छलाँग लगाता है,
मैंने शिकारी को कहते सुना है;
passages.bn:
আহত হরিণই সবচেয়ে উঁচুতে লাফায়,
শিকারির মুখে শুনেছি;
passages.id:
Rusa yang terluka melompat paling tinggi,
begitu kudengar sang pemburu berkata;
passages.tr:
Yaralı geyik en yükseğe sıçrar,
avcının söylediğini duydum;
passages.vi:
Con hươu bị thương nhảy cao nhất,
tôi đã nghe người thợ săn nói vậy;
passages.th:
กวางบาดเจ็บกระโดดได้สูงที่สุด
ฉันเคยได้ยินนายพรานบอกไว้

entries.passageOriginal:
The soul selects her own society,
Then shuts the door;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: The soul selects her own society
entries.englishWorkTitle: The soul selects her own society
entries.englishContextNote: The soul is personified as deliberately choosing its intimacies and then protecting that choice.

passages.en:
The soul selects her own society,
Then shuts the door;
passages.zh-Hans:
灵魂选择自己的同伴，
然后把门关上；
passages.zh-Hant:
靈魂選擇自己的同伴，
然後把門關上；
passages.ja:
魂は自ら仲間を選び、
それから扉を閉じる。
passages.ko:
영혼은 스스로 자신의 벗을 고르고,
그런 다음 문을 닫는다.
passages.es:
El alma elige su propia compañía,
y luego cierra la puerta;
passages.fr:
L’âme choisit sa propre compagnie,
puis ferme la porte ;
passages.de:
Die Seele wählt ihre eigene Gesellschaft,
dann schließt sie die Tür;
passages.it:
L’anima sceglie la propria compagnia,
poi chiude la porta;
passages.pt:
A alma escolhe sua própria companhia,
e então fecha a porta;
passages.ru:
Душа сама избирает свой круг,
а затем закрывает дверь;
passages.sv:
Själen väljer sitt eget sällskap,
och stänger sedan dörren;
passages.ar:
تختار الروح صحبتها بنفسها،
ثم تغلق الباب؛
passages.hi:
आत्मा अपना समाज स्वयं चुनती है,
फिर द्वार बंद कर देती है;
passages.bn:
আত্মা নিজের সঙ্গ নিজেই বেছে নেয়,
তারপর দরজা বন্ধ করে;
passages.id:
Jiwa memilih pergaulannya sendiri,
lalu menutup pintu;
passages.tr:
Ruh kendi çevresini seçer,
sonra kapıyı kapatır;
passages.vi:
Tâm hồn tự chọn những người đồng hành,
rồi khép cửa lại;
passages.th:
จิตวิญญาณเลือกสังคมของตนเอง
แล้วจึงปิดประตู

entries.passageOriginal:
This is my letter to the world,
That never wrote to me, —
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: This is my letter to the world
entries.englishWorkTitle: This is my letter to the world
entries.englishContextNote: The poem frames itself as an unrequested communication sent outward despite the world’s silence.

passages.en:
This is my letter to the world,
That never wrote to me, —
passages.zh-Hans:
这是我写给世界的信，
它从未给我来信——
passages.zh-Hant:
這是我寫給世界的信，
它從未給我來信——
passages.ja:
これは世界への私の手紙、
私には一度も書いてこなかった世界へ——
passages.ko:
이것은 세상에 보내는 나의 편지,
내게 한 번도 편지하지 않은 세상에—
passages.es:
Esta es mi carta al mundo,
que nunca me escribió, —
passages.fr:
Voici ma lettre au monde,
qui ne m’a jamais écrit, —
passages.de:
Dies ist mein Brief an die Welt,
die mir niemals schrieb, —
passages.it:
Questa è la mia lettera al mondo,
che non mi ha mai scritto, —
passages.pt:
Esta é minha carta ao mundo,
que nunca escreveu para mim, —
passages.ru:
Вот моё письмо миру,
который мне никогда не писал, —
passages.sv:
Detta är mitt brev till världen,
som aldrig skrev till mig, —
passages.ar:
هذه رسالتي إلى العالم،
الذي لم يكتب إليّ قط، —
passages.hi:
यह संसार को मेरा पत्र है,
जिसने मुझे कभी नहीं लिखा, —
passages.bn:
এ আমার চিঠি পৃথিবীর কাছে,
যে কখনও আমাকে লেখেনি—
passages.id:
Inilah suratku kepada dunia,
yang tak pernah menulis kepadaku, —
passages.tr:
Bu, dünyaya yazdığım mektup,
bana hiç yazmamış olan dünyaya—
passages.vi:
Đây là lá thư tôi gửi thế gian,
nơi chưa từng viết cho tôi, —
passages.th:
นี่คือจดหมายของฉันถึงโลก
โลกที่ไม่เคยเขียนถึงฉันเลย—

entries.passageOriginal:
I taste a liquor never brewed,
From tankards scooped in pearl;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: I taste a liquor never brewed
entries.englishWorkTitle: I taste a liquor never brewed
entries.englishContextNote: The opening turns delight in air, dew, and summer into the imagery of an impossible drink.

passages.en:
I taste a liquor never brewed,
From tankards scooped in pearl;
passages.zh-Hans:
我尝到一种从未酿造的酒，
盛在珍珠凿成的杯中；
passages.zh-Hant:
我嚐到一種從未釀造的酒，
盛在珍珠鑿成的杯中；
passages.ja:
醸されたことのない酒を味わう、
真珠をくり抜いた杯から。
passages.ko:
한 번도 빚은 적 없는 술을 맛본다,
진주를 파 만든 잔에서.
passages.es:
Pruebo un licor nunca destilado,
en jarras talladas de perla;
passages.fr:
Je goûte une liqueur jamais brassée,
dans des cruches taillées dans la perle ;
passages.de:
Ich koste einen Trank, der nie gebraut ward,
aus Humpen, aus Perlen gehöhlt;
passages.it:
Assaggio un liquore mai distillato,
da coppe scavate nella perla;
passages.pt:
Provo um licor jamais fabricado,
em canecas talhadas de pérola;
passages.ru:
Я пробую напиток, что не варили,
из кружек, выточенных из жемчуга;
passages.sv:
Jag smakar en dryck som aldrig bryggts,
ur bägare urholkade i pärla;
passages.ar:
أتذوق شراباً لم يُخمّر قط،
من أقداح منحوتة من اللؤلؤ؛
passages.hi:
मैं ऐसी मदिरा चखती हूँ जो कभी बनी नहीं,
मोती से तराशे प्यालों में;
passages.bn:
আমি চাখি এমন পানীয় যা কখনও তৈরি হয়নি,
মুক্তো কেটে বানানো পেয়ালা থেকে;
passages.id:
Kucicipi minuman yang tak pernah diramu,
dari cawan yang dipahat dari mutiara;
passages.tr:
Hiç mayalanmamış bir içkiyi tadarım,
inciden oyulmuş kupalardan;
passages.vi:
Tôi nếm thứ rượu chưa từng được ủ,
từ những cốc khoét trong ngọc trai;
passages.th:
ฉันลิ้มรสสุราที่ไม่เคยถูกหมัก
จากถ้วยที่เจาะจากไข่มุก

entries.passageOriginal:
He ate and drank the precious words,
His spirit grew robust;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: Reading is figured as nourishment that gives strength to a spirit otherwise constrained by poverty and mortality.

passages.en:
He ate and drank the precious words,
His spirit grew robust;
passages.zh-Hans:
他吃下、饮下那些珍贵的词语，
他的精神变得强健；
passages.zh-Hant:
他吃下、飲下那些珍貴的詞語，
他的精神變得強健；
passages.ja:
彼は尊い言葉を食べ、飲み、
その精神はたくましくなった。
passages.ko:
그는 귀한 말들을 먹고 마셨고,
그의 정신은 튼튼해졌다.
passages.es:
Comió y bebió las preciosas palabras,
y su espíritu se fortaleció;
passages.fr:
Il mangea et but les mots précieux,
son esprit devint robuste ;
passages.de:
Er aß und trank die kostbaren Worte,
sein Geist wurde stark;
passages.it:
Mangiò e bevve le preziose parole,
il suo spirito si fece robusto;
passages.pt:
Ele comeu e bebeu as palavras preciosas,
seu espírito ficou forte;
passages.ru:
Он ел и пил драгоценные слова,
и дух его окреп;
passages.sv:
Han åt och drack de dyrbara orden,
hans ande blev stark;
passages.ar:
أكل الكلمات النفيسة وشربها،
فقويت روحه؛
passages.hi:
उसने अनमोल शब्द खाए और पिए,
उसकी आत्मा सुदृढ़ हुई;
passages.bn:
সে মূল্যবান শব্দগুলো খেল ও পান করল,
তার আত্মা সবল হয়ে উঠল;
passages.id:
Ia makan dan minum kata-kata berharga,
jiwanya menjadi kuat;
passages.tr:
Değerli sözleri yiyip içti,
ruhu güçlendi;
passages.vi:
Người ấy ăn uống những lời quý giá,
tinh thần trở nên mạnh mẽ;
passages.th:
เขากินและดื่มถ้อยคำล้ำค่า
จิตวิญญาณของเขาจึงแข็งแรงขึ้น

entries.passageOriginal:
I had no time to hate, because
The grave would hinder me,
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: I had no time to hate, because
entries.englishWorkTitle: I had no time to hate, because
entries.englishContextNote: The brevity of life becomes a practical reason not to spend its limited time sustaining hatred.

passages.en:
I had no time to hate, because
The grave would hinder me,
passages.zh-Hans:
我没有时间去恨，因为
坟墓会把我阻断，
passages.zh-Hant:
我沒有時間去恨，因為
墳墓會把我阻斷，
passages.ja:
憎む時間はなかった、なぜなら
墓が私を妨げるから。
passages.ko:
미워할 시간이 없었다, 왜냐하면
무덤이 나를 가로막을 테니,
passages.es:
No tuve tiempo para odiar, porque
la tumba me lo impediría,
passages.fr:
Je n’avais pas le temps de haïr, car
la tombe m’en empêcherait,
passages.de:
Ich hatte keine Zeit zu hassen, denn
das Grab würde mich hindern,
passages.it:
Non avevo tempo per odiare, perché
la tomba me lo avrebbe impedito,
passages.pt:
Não tive tempo para odiar, porque
o túmulo me impediria,
passages.ru:
Мне некогда было ненавидеть, ведь
могила помешала бы мне,
passages.sv:
Jag hade ingen tid att hata, ty
graven skulle hindra mig,
passages.ar:
لم يكن لدي وقت للكراهية، لأن
القبر سيمنعني،
passages.hi:
मेरे पास घृणा का समय न था, क्योंकि
कब्र मुझे रोक देती,
passages.bn:
ঘৃণা করার সময় আমার ছিল না, কারণ
কবর আমাকে থামিয়ে দিত,
passages.id:
Aku tak punya waktu untuk membenci, sebab
kubur akan menghalangiku,
passages.tr:
Nefret etmeye vaktim yoktu, çünkü
mezar beni engellerdi,
passages.vi:
Tôi không có thời gian để ghét, vì
nấm mồ sẽ ngăn tôi lại,
passages.th:
ฉันไม่มีเวลาจะเกลียด เพราะ
หลุมศพจะขัดขวางฉัน

entries.passageOriginal:
I never saw a moor,
I never saw the sea;
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: The speaker begins from what she has not witnessed before asserting the reality of knowledge and belief beyond direct sight.

passages.en:
I never saw a moor,
I never saw the sea;
passages.zh-Hans:
我从未见过荒原，
我从未见过大海；
passages.zh-Hant:
我從未見過荒原，
我從未見過大海；
passages.ja:
荒野を見たことはない、
海を見たこともない。
passages.ko:
나는 황야를 본 적 없고,
바다도 본 적 없다.
passages.es:
Nunca vi un páramo,
nunca vi el mar;
passages.fr:
Je n’ai jamais vu de lande,
je n’ai jamais vu la mer ;
passages.de:
Ich sah niemals eine Heide,
ich sah niemals das Meer;
passages.it:
Non vidi mai una brughiera,
non vidi mai il mare;
passages.pt:
Nunca vi uma charneca,
nunca vi o mar;
passages.ru:
Я никогда не видела пустоши,
никогда не видела моря;
passages.sv:
Jag såg aldrig en hed,
jag såg aldrig havet;
passages.ar:
لم أرَ قط أرضاً برية،
ولم أرَ البحر قط؛
passages.hi:
मैंने कभी बंजर मैदान नहीं देखा,
मैंने कभी समुद्र नहीं देखा;
passages.bn:
আমি কখনও প্রান্তর দেখিনি,
কখনও সমুদ্র দেখিনি;
passages.id:
Aku tak pernah melihat padang tandus,
aku tak pernah melihat laut;
passages.tr:
Hiç kır görmedim,
hiç deniz görmedim;
passages.vi:
Tôi chưa từng thấy đồng hoang,
chưa từng thấy biển;
passages.th:
ฉันไม่เคยเห็นทุ่งร้าง
ฉันไม่เคยเห็นทะเล

entries.passageOriginal:
Elysium is as far as to
The very nearest room,
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: Paradise is measured not as a remote realm but as the small distance to a nearby room where news may wait.

passages.en:
Elysium is as far as to
The very nearest room,
passages.zh-Hans:
极乐之境的距离，不过是
走到最近的房间，
passages.zh-Hant:
極樂之境的距離，不過是
走到最近的房間，
passages.ja:
楽園までの距離は
いちばん近い部屋までほど、
passages.ko:
낙원까지의 거리는
가장 가까운 방까지일 뿐,
passages.es:
El Elíseo está tan lejos como
la habitación más cercana,
passages.fr:
L’Élysée n’est pas plus loin que
la chambre la plus proche,
passages.de:
Elysium ist nur so weit wie
das allernächste Zimmer,
passages.it:
L’Elisio è lontano quanto
la stanza più vicina,
passages.pt:
O Elísio fica tão longe quanto
o quarto mais próximo,
passages.ru:
До Элизиума не дальше, чем
до самой ближней комнаты,
passages.sv:
Elysium är inte längre bort än
det allra närmaste rummet,
passages.ar:
الإليزيوم ليس أبعد من
أقرب غرفة،
passages.hi:
स्वर्ग उतना ही दूर है जितना
बिलकुल पास का कमरा,
passages.bn:
স্বর্গ ততটাই দূরে যতটা
একেবারে কাছের ঘরটি,
passages.id:
Elysium hanya sejauh
ruang yang paling dekat,
passages.tr:
Elysium ancak
en yakın oda kadar uzaktır,
passages.vi:
Cõi cực lạc chỉ xa bằng
căn phòng gần nhất,
passages.th:
แดนสุขาวดีอยู่ไกลเพียง
ห้องที่ใกล้ที่สุด

entries.passageOriginal:
Have you got a brook in your little heart,
Where bashful flowers blow,
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.originalWorkTitle: Have you got a brook in your little heart
entries.englishWorkTitle: Have you got a brook in your little heart
entries.englishContextNote: An inward life is imagined as a private stream where delicate forms of growth can appear.

passages.en:
Have you got a brook in your little heart,
Where bashful flowers blow,
passages.zh-Hans:
你小小的心里是否有一条溪流，
羞怯的花在那里开放，
passages.zh-Hant:
你小小的心裡是否有一條溪流，
羞怯的花在那裡開放，
passages.ja:
あなたの小さな心には小川がある？
恥ずかしげな花が咲くところ、
passages.ko:
당신의 작은 마음에는 시냇물이 있나요,
수줍은 꽃들이 피어나는 곳,
passages.es:
¿Tienes un arroyo en tu pequeño corazón,
donde florecen tímidas flores,
passages.fr:
As-tu un ruisseau dans ton petit cœur,
où s’ouvrent des fleurs timides,
passages.de:
Hast du einen Bach in deinem kleinen Herzen,
wo schüchterne Blumen blühen,
passages.it:
Hai un ruscello nel tuo piccolo cuore,
dove sbocciano fiori timidi,
passages.pt:
Há um riacho em teu pequeno coração,
onde flores tímidas desabrocham,
passages.ru:
Есть ли ручей в твоём маленьком сердце,
где распускаются робкие цветы,
passages.sv:
Har du en bäck i ditt lilla hjärta,
där blyga blommor slår ut,
passages.ar:
هل في قلبك الصغير جدول،
تتفتح عنده أزهار خجولة،
passages.hi:
क्या तुम्हारे छोटे से हृदय में कोई धारा है,
जहाँ संकोची फूल खिलते हैं,
passages.bn:
তোমার ছোট্ট হৃদয়ে কি একটি ঝরনা আছে,
যেখানে লাজুক ফুল ফোটে,
passages.id:
Adakah sungai kecil di dalam hatimu,
tempat bunga-bunga malu bermekaran,
passages.tr:
Küçük kalbinde bir dere var mı,
utangaç çiçeklerin açtığı,
passages.vi:
Trong trái tim nhỏ của bạn có dòng suối không,
nơi những bông hoa e lệ nở,
passages.th:
ในหัวใจดวงน้อยของเธอมีลำธารไหม
ที่ซึ่งดอกไม้อาย ๆ ผลิบาน

entries.passageOriginal:
No rack can torture me,
My soul's at liberty
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: The speaker opposes bodily coercion with an inner freedom that cannot be reached by instruments of pain.

passages.en:
No rack can torture me,
My soul's at liberty
passages.zh-Hans:
没有刑架能折磨我，
我的灵魂是自由的
passages.zh-Hant:
沒有刑架能折磨我，
我的靈魂是自由的
passages.ja:
どんな拷問台も私を苦しめられない、
私の魂は自由だから
passages.ko:
어떤 고문대도 나를 괴롭힐 수 없다,
내 영혼은 자유로우니
passages.es:
Ningún potro puede torturarme,
mi alma está en libertad
passages.fr:
Aucun chevalet ne peut me torturer,
mon âme est libre
passages.de:
Keine Folterbank kann mich quälen,
meine Seele ist frei
passages.it:
Nessun cavalletto può torturarmi,
la mia anima è libera
passages.pt:
Nenhum instrumento pode me torturar,
minha alma está livre
passages.ru:
Никакая дыба меня не измучит,
моя душа свободна
passages.sv:
Ingen sträckbänk kan plåga mig,
min själ är fri
passages.ar:
لا آلة تعذيب تستطيع إيذائي،
فروحي حرة
passages.hi:
कोई यातना-यंत्र मुझे नहीं सता सकता,
मेरी आत्मा स्वतंत्र है
passages.bn:
কোনো নির্যাতনযন্ত্র আমাকে কষ্ট দিতে পারে না,
আমার আত্মা স্বাধীন
passages.id:
Tak ada alat penyiksa yang dapat menyiksaku,
jiwaku merdeka
passages.tr:
Hiçbir işkence sehpası bana eziyet edemez,
ruhum özgürdür
passages.vi:
Không giá tra tấn nào hành hạ được tôi,
tâm hồn tôi tự do
passages.th:
ไม่มีเครื่องทรมานใดทำร้ายฉันได้
วิญญาณของฉันเป็นอิสระ

entries.passageOriginal:
Nature, like us, is sometimes caught
Without her diadem.
entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.englishContextNote: A dull winter sky becomes a reminder that even nature is not always encountered in ceremonial beauty.

passages.en:
Nature, like us, is sometimes caught
Without her diadem.
passages.zh-Hans:
自然也像我们，有时会被撞见
没有戴上她的冠冕。
passages.zh-Hant:
自然也像我們，有時會被撞見
沒有戴上她的冠冕。
passages.ja:
自然も私たちと同じく、ときには
冠をつけない姿を見られる。
passages.ko:
자연도 우리처럼 때로는
왕관을 쓰지 않은 채 들킨다.
passages.es:
La naturaleza, como nosotros, a veces es sorprendida
sin su diadema.
passages.fr:
La nature, comme nous, est parfois surprise
sans son diadème.
passages.de:
Die Natur wird, wie wir, bisweilen
ohne ihr Diadem angetroffen.
passages.it:
La natura, come noi, talvolta è sorpresa
senza il suo diadema.
passages.pt:
A natureza, como nós, às vezes é surpreendida
sem seu diadema.
passages.ru:
Природу, как и нас, порой застают
без её диадемы.
passages.sv:
Naturen blir, liksom vi, ibland påkommen
utan sitt diadem.
passages.ar:
الطبيعة مثلنا، تُفاجأ أحياناً
من دون تاجها.
passages.hi:
प्रकृति भी हमारी तरह कभी-कभी
अपने मुकुट के बिना मिलती है।
passages.bn:
প্রকৃতিও আমাদের মতো কখনও কখনও
মুকুটহীন অবস্থায় ধরা পড়ে।
passages.id:
Alam, seperti kita, terkadang didapati
tanpa mahkotanya.
passages.tr:
Doğa da bizim gibi bazen
tacı olmadan yakalanır.
passages.vi:
Thiên nhiên, như chúng ta, đôi khi bị bắt gặp
không đội vương miện.
passages.th:
ธรรมชาติก็เหมือนเรา บางครั้งถูกพบเห็น
โดยปราศจากมงกุฎของเธอ

entries.passageOriginal:
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high;
Where knowledge is free;
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: the poem imagines a country awakened into intellectual freedom, candour, and fearless dignity.

passages.en:
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high;
Where knowledge is free;
passages.zh-Hans:
在那里，心无畏惧，头颅高昂；
在那里，知识自由；
passages.zh-Hant:
在那裡，心無畏懼，頭顱高昂；
在那裡，知識自由；
passages.ja:
心に恐れがなく、頭が高く掲げられるところ、
知識が自由なところ、
passages.ko:
마음에 두려움이 없고 머리를 높이 드는 곳,
지식이 자유로운 곳,
passages.es:
Donde la mente no teme y la cabeza se alza;
donde el conocimiento es libre;
passages.fr:
Là où l'esprit est sans peur et la tête haute ;
là où le savoir est libre ;
passages.de:
Wo der Geist ohne Furcht ist und das Haupt erhoben;
wo Wissen frei ist;
passages.it:
Dove la mente è senza paura e il capo è alto;
dove il sapere è libero;
passages.pt:
Onde a mente não tem medo e a cabeça se ergue;
onde o saber é livre;
passages.ru:
Где разум не знает страха и голова поднята высоко;
где знание свободно;
passages.sv:
Där sinnet är utan fruktan och huvudet hålls högt;
där kunskapen är fri;
passages.ar:
حيث العقل بلا خوف والرأس مرفوع؛
حيث المعرفة حرة؛
passages.hi:
जहाँ मन भय से मुक्त हो और मस्तक ऊँचा रहे;
जहाँ ज्ञान स्वतंत्र हो;
passages.bn:
চিত্ত যেথা ভয়শূন্য, উচ্চ যেথা শির;
জ্ঞান যেথা মুক্ত;
passages.id:
Di mana pikiran bebas dari takut dan kepala tegak;
di mana pengetahuan bebas;
passages.tr:
Zihnin korkusuz, başın dik olduğu yerde;
bilginin özgür olduğu yerde;
passages.vi:
Nơi tâm trí không sợ hãi và đầu ngẩng cao;
nơi tri thức được tự do;
passages.th:
ที่ซึ่งจิตใจไร้ความกลัวและศีรษะเชิดสูง
ที่ซึ่งความรู้เป็นอิสระ

entries.passageOriginal:
When old words die out on the tongue, new melodies break forth from the heart;
and where the old tracks are lost, new country is revealed with its wonders.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: at the apparent end of a journey, the speaker discovers renewal beyond exhausted language and vanished roads.

passages.en:
When old words die out on the tongue, new melodies break forth from the heart;
and where the old tracks are lost, new country is revealed with its wonders.
passages.zh-Hans:
当旧日言语消逝于舌尖，新的旋律便从心中涌出；
当旧路隐没，新的国度便显露它的奇景。
passages.zh-Hant:
當舊日言語消逝於舌尖，新的旋律便從心中湧出；
當舊路隱沒，新的國度便顯露它的奇景。
passages.ja:
古い言葉が舌の上で尽きると、新しい調べが心から湧き出す。
古い道が消えたところに、驚異に満ちた新しい国が現れる。
passages.ko:
낡은 말이 혀끝에서 사라지면 새 선율이 마음에서 솟고,
옛길이 끊긴 곳에서 경이로운 새 땅이 드러난다.
passages.es:
Cuando mueren las viejas palabras, brotan del corazón melodías nuevas;
y donde se pierden las viejas sendas, aparece una tierra nueva y prodigiosa.
passages.fr:
Quand les vieux mots meurent sur la langue, de nouvelles mélodies jaillissent du cœur ;
et là où les anciennes pistes se perdent, un pays nouveau révèle ses merveilles.
passages.de:
Wenn alte Worte auf der Zunge sterben, brechen neue Melodien aus dem Herzen hervor;
und wo alte Pfade verschwinden, zeigt sich neues Land voller Wunder.
passages.it:
Quando le vecchie parole muoiono sulla lingua, nuove melodie sgorgano dal cuore;
e dove si perdono le vecchie vie, si rivela una terra nuova e meravigliosa.
passages.pt:
Quando velhas palavras morrem na língua, novas melodias irrompem do coração;
e onde se perdem os velhos caminhos, revela-se uma terra nova com suas maravilhas.
passages.ru:
Когда старые слова умирают на языке, из сердца вырываются новые мелодии;
а там, где теряются старые пути, открывается новая страна чудес.
passages.sv:
När gamla ord dör på tungan bryter nya melodier fram ur hjärtat;
och där gamla spår försvinner visar sig ett nytt land med sina under.
passages.ar:
حين تموت الكلمات القديمة على اللسان، تنبثق ألحان جديدة من القلب؛
وحيث تضيع الدروب القديمة، تنكشف أرض جديدة بعجائبها.
passages.hi:
जब पुराने शब्द जिह्वा पर मर जाते हैं, हृदय से नई धुनें फूटती हैं;
और जहाँ पुराने रास्ते खो जाते हैं, वहाँ अपने चमत्कारों सहित नया देश खुलता है।
passages.bn:
পুরোনো কথা জিহ্বায় মরে গেলে হৃদয় থেকে নতুন সুর ফোটে;
আর পুরোনো পথ হারালে বিস্ময় নিয়ে নতুন দেশ দেখা দেয়।
passages.id:
Saat kata lama mati di lidah, melodi baru memancar dari hati;
dan ketika jejak lama hilang, negeri baru menyingkap keajaibannya.
passages.tr:
Eski sözler dilde ölünce kalpten yeni ezgiler doğar;
eski yollar kaybolunca mucizeleriyle yeni bir ülke belirir.
passages.vi:
Khi lời cũ tắt trên đầu lưỡi, giai điệu mới bật lên từ tim;
và nơi lối xưa mất dấu, miền đất mới hiện ra cùng bao kỳ diệu.
passages.th:
เมื่อถ้อยคำเก่าดับลงบนลิ้น ท่วงทำนองใหม่ก็ผุดจากหัวใจ
และเมื่อทางเก่าสูญหาย ดินแดนใหม่ก็เผยสิ่งมหัศจรรย์

entries.passageOriginal:
I am restless. I am athirst for far-away things.
My soul goes out in a longing to touch the skirt of the dim distance.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: restlessness becomes a desire to reach beyond the familiar toward a distance that cannot yet be clearly seen.

passages.en:
I am restless. I am athirst for far-away things.
My soul goes out in a longing to touch the skirt of the dim distance.
passages.zh-Hans:
我不得安宁。我渴望遥远的事物。
我的灵魂出发了，渴望触到朦胧远方的衣角。
passages.zh-Hant:
我不得安寧。我渴望遙遠的事物。
我的靈魂出發了，渴望觸到朦朧遠方的衣角。
passages.ja:
私は落ち着かない。遠いものに渇いている。
私の魂は、霞む遠方の裾に触れたいと旅立つ。
passages.ko:
나는 안절부절못한다. 먼 것들에 목마르다.
내 영혼은 흐릿한 먼 곳의 옷자락을 만지고자 나아간다.
passages.es:
Estoy inquieto. Tengo sed de cosas lejanas.
Mi alma sale anhelando tocar el borde de la distancia borrosa.
passages.fr:
Je suis inquiet. J'ai soif des choses lointaines.
Mon âme s'élance, désirant toucher le bord du lointain brumeux.
passages.de:
Ich bin ruhelos. Mich dürstet nach fernen Dingen.
Meine Seele zieht aus, um den Saum der dämmernden Ferne zu berühren.
passages.it:
Sono inquieto. Ho sete di cose lontane.
La mia anima si protende per toccare il lembo della distanza velata.
passages.pt:
Estou inquieto. Tenho sede de coisas distantes.
Minha alma parte, desejando tocar a orla da distância enevoada.
passages.ru:
Я беспокоен. Я жажду далёкого.
Моя душа устремляется коснуться края туманной дали.
passages.sv:
Jag är rastlös. Jag törstar efter fjärran ting.
Min själ sträcker sig efter att röra vid den dunkla horisontens fåll.
passages.ar:
أنا قلق، وعطشان إلى الأشياء البعيدة.
تنطلق روحي شوقاً إلى لمس طرف المسافة الضبابية.
passages.hi:
मैं बेचैन हूँ। मैं दूर की वस्तुओं का प्यासा हूँ।
मेरी आत्मा धुँधली दूरी का आँचल छूने की लालसा में निकलती है।
passages.bn:
আমি চঞ্চল। দূরের জিনিসের জন্য আমি তৃষ্ণার্ত।
অস্পষ্ট দূরত্বের আঁচল ছুঁতে আমার আত্মা আকুল হয়ে বেরিয়ে পড়ে।
passages.id:
Aku gelisah. Aku haus akan hal-hal yang jauh.
Jiwaku pergi, rindu menyentuh ujung kejauhan yang samar.
passages.tr:
Huzursuzum. Uzak şeylere susadım.
Ruhum, puslu uzaklığın eteğine dokunma özlemiyle yola çıkıyor.
passages.vi:
Tôi bồn chồn. Tôi khát những điều xa xôi.
Hồn tôi vươn đi, mong chạm vào vạt áo của miền xa mờ.
passages.th:
ฉันกระสับกระส่าย ฉันกระหายสิ่งที่อยู่ไกล
วิญญาณฉันออกไปด้วยความปรารถนาจะสัมผัสชายขอบของระยะทางพร่ามัว

entries.passageOriginal:
In the world's audience hall, the simple blade of grass sits on the same carpet
with the sunbeam and the stars of midnight.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: a blade of grass is placed beside cosmic light, giving the smallest life an equal place in the world's assembly.

passages.en:
In the world's audience hall, the simple blade of grass sits on the same carpet
with the sunbeam and the stars of midnight.
passages.zh-Hans:
在世界的大厅里，一片平凡的草叶坐在同一张地毯上，
与阳光和午夜的星辰同席。
passages.zh-Hant:
在世界的大廳裡，一片平凡的草葉坐在同一張地毯上，
與陽光和午夜的星辰同席。
passages.ja:
世界の広間では、名もない草の葉が同じ絨毯に座る。
陽の光や真夜中の星々とともに。
passages.ko:
세상의 회당에서 소박한 풀잎은 같은 융단에 앉는다.
햇살과 한밤의 별들과 함께.
passages.es:
En la sala del mundo, la sencilla brizna se sienta en la misma alfombra
que el rayo de sol y las estrellas de medianoche.
passages.fr:
Dans la salle du monde, le simple brin d'herbe s'assied sur le même tapis
que le rayon de soleil et les étoiles de minuit.
passages.de:
Im Saal der Welt sitzt der schlichte Grashalm auf demselben Teppich
wie der Sonnenstrahl und die Sterne der Mitternacht.
passages.it:
Nella sala del mondo, il semplice filo d'erba siede sullo stesso tappeto
del raggio di sole e delle stelle di mezzanotte.
passages.pt:
No salão do mundo, a simples folha de relva senta-se no mesmo tapete
que o raio de sol e as estrelas da meia-noite.
passages.ru:
В зале мира простая травинка сидит на одном ковре
с солнечным лучом и полуночными звёздами.
passages.sv:
I världens sal sitter det enkla grässtrået på samma matta
som solstrålen och midnattens stjärnor.
passages.ar:
في قاعة العالم تجلس نبتة العشب البسيطة على البساط نفسه
مع شعاع الشمس ونجوم منتصف الليل.
passages.hi:
विश्व के सभा-भवन में साधारण घास की पत्ती उसी कालीन पर बैठती है
जहाँ धूप की किरण और आधी रात के तारे।
passages.bn:
বিশ্বের সভাঘরে সাধারণ ঘাসের পাতা একই গালিচায় বসে
সূর্যকিরণ আর মধ্যরাতের তারাদের সঙ্গে।
passages.id:
Di balairung dunia, sehelai rumput sederhana duduk di karpet yang sama
dengan sinar matahari dan bintang tengah malam.
passages.tr:
Dünyanın salonunda sade bir çim yaprağı aynı halıda oturur,
güneş ışını ve gece yarısı yıldızlarıyla.
passages.vi:
Trong đại sảnh của thế gian, ngọn cỏ đơn sơ ngồi trên cùng tấm thảm
với tia nắng và những vì sao nửa đêm.
passages.th:
ในท้องพระโรงของโลก ใบหญ้าธรรมดานั่งบนพรมผืนเดียวกัน
กับแสงอาทิตย์และดวงดาวยามเที่ยงคืน

entries.passageOriginal:
THE world puts off its mask of vastness to its lover.
It becomes small as one song, as one kiss of the eternal.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: love changes the world's overwhelming scale into something intimate enough to be held in a song or kiss.

passages.en:
THE world puts off its mask of vastness to its lover.
It becomes small as one song, as one kiss of the eternal.
passages.zh-Hans:
世界向它的爱人摘下浩瀚的面具。
它变得如一支歌那样小，如永恒的一吻。
passages.zh-Hant:
世界向它的愛人摘下浩瀚的面具。
它變得如一支歌那樣小，如永恆的一吻。
passages.ja:
世界は愛する者に、広大さの仮面を脱ぐ。
一つの歌ほど、一つの永遠の口づけほど小さくなる。
passages.ko:
세계는 사랑하는 이 앞에서 광대함의 가면을 벗는다.
한 노래처럼, 영원의 한 입맞춤처럼 작아진다.
passages.es:
El mundo se quita ante quien lo ama su máscara de inmensidad.
Se vuelve pequeño como una canción, como un beso de lo eterno.
passages.fr:
Le monde ôte son masque d'immensité devant qui l'aime.
Il devient petit comme un chant, comme un baiser de l'éternel.
passages.de:
Die Welt legt vor ihrem Liebenden die Maske der Weite ab.
Sie wird klein wie ein Lied, wie ein Kuss des Ewigen.
passages.it:
Il mondo depone davanti a chi lo ama la maschera dell'immensità.
Diventa piccolo come un canto, come un bacio dell'eterno.
passages.pt:
O mundo tira diante de quem o ama a máscara da vastidão.
Torna-se pequeno como uma canção, como um beijo do eterno.
passages.ru:
Мир снимает перед любящим маску необъятности.
Он становится мал, как песня, как поцелуй вечности.
passages.sv:
Världen tar av sig väldighetens mask inför den som älskar den.
Den blir liten som en sång, som en kyss från evigheten.
passages.ar:
ينزع العالم قناع اتساعه أمام من يحبه.
فيصغر كأغنية، كقبلة من الأبدية.
passages.hi:
संसार अपने प्रेमी के सामने विराटता का मुखौटा उतार देता है।
वह एक गीत जितना छोटा, अनंत के एक चुंबन जैसा हो जाता है।
passages.bn:
বিশ্ব তার প্রেমিকের কাছে বিশালতার মুখোশ খুলে ফেলে।
সে হয়ে ওঠে একটি গানের মতো ছোট, অনন্তের একটি চুম্বনের মতো।
passages.id:
Dunia menanggalkan topeng keluasannya di hadapan kekasihnya.
Ia menjadi kecil seperti sebuah lagu, seperti satu ciuman keabadian.
passages.tr:
Dünya, onu sevenin önünde enginlik maskesini çıkarır.
Bir şarkı, sonsuzluğun bir öpücüğü kadar küçülür.
passages.vi:
Thế gian tháo chiếc mặt nạ mênh mông trước người yêu nó.
Nó nhỏ lại như một bài ca, như một nụ hôn của vĩnh hằng.
passages.th:
โลกถอดหน้ากากแห่งความไพศาลต่อหน้าผู้รักมัน
มันเล็กลงดังบทเพลงหนึ่ง ดั่งจุมพิตหนึ่งของนิรันดร์

entries.passageOriginal:
ONCE we dreamt that we were strangers.
We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: estrangement is recast as a passing dream, while waking reveals an affection that was already present.

passages.en:
ONCE we dreamt that we were strangers.
We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.
passages.zh-Hans:
我们曾梦见彼此陌生。
醒来才发现，我们原来相亲相爱。
passages.zh-Hant:
我們曾夢見彼此陌生。
醒來才發現，我們原來相親相愛。
passages.ja:
かつて私たちは他人だと夢見ていた。
目覚めると、互いに大切な者だったと知る。
passages.ko:
우리는 한때 서로 낯선 사람이라고 꿈꾸었다.
깨어 보니 서로 소중한 사이였다.
passages.es:
Una vez soñamos que éramos extraños.
Despertamos y descubrimos que nos queríamos.
passages.fr:
Un jour, nous avons rêvé que nous étions étrangers.
Nous nous réveillons et découvrons que nous nous étions chers.
passages.de:
Einst träumten wir, wir seien Fremde.
Wir erwachen und sehen, dass wir einander lieb waren.
passages.it:
Un tempo sognammo di essere estranei.
Ci svegliamo e scopriamo di esserci cari.
passages.pt:
Certa vez sonhamos que éramos estranhos.
Despertamos e descobrimos que éramos queridos um ao outro.
passages.ru:
Однажды нам приснилось, что мы чужие.
Мы проснулись и поняли, что дороги друг другу.
passages.sv:
En gång drömde vi att vi var främlingar.
Vi vaknar och finner att vi var varandra kära.
passages.ar:
حلمنا ذات مرة أننا غريبان.
استيقظنا فوجدنا أننا عزيزان أحدنا على الآخر.
passages.hi:
कभी हमने सपना देखा कि हम अजनबी थे।
जागे तो पाया कि हम एक-दूसरे को प्रिय थे।
passages.bn:
একদিন স্বপ্ন দেখেছিলাম আমরা অচেনা।
জেগে দেখি আমরা পরস্পরের প্রিয়।
passages.id:
Pernah kita bermimpi bahwa kita orang asing.
Kita terbangun dan tahu bahwa kita saling menyayangi.
passages.tr:
Bir zamanlar yabancı olduğumuzu düşledik.
Uyandık ve birbirimize değerli olduğumuzu gördük.
passages.vi:
Có lần ta mơ mình là người xa lạ.
Tỉnh dậy mới hay ta vốn quý mến nhau.
passages.th:
ครั้งหนึ่งเราฝันว่าเราเป็นคนแปลกหน้า
เมื่อตื่นขึ้นจึงพบว่าเราต่างเป็นที่รักของกันและกัน

entries.passageOriginal:
My life when young was like a flower—a flower that loosens a petal or two from her abundance
and never feels the loss when the spring breeze comes to beg at her door.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: youth is pictured as a flower able to give freely from abundance without measuring what has been lost.

passages.en:
My life when young was like a flower—a flower that loosens a petal or two from her abundance
and never feels the loss when the spring breeze comes to beg at her door.
passages.zh-Hans:
我年轻时的生命像一朵花——从丰盛中松落一两片花瓣，
当春风来到门前求取时，从不觉得有所损失。
passages.zh-Hant:
我年輕時的生命像一朵花——從豐盛中鬆落一兩片花瓣，
當春風來到門前求取時，從不覺得有所損失。
passages.ja:
若い日の私の命は花のようだった——豊かさから花びらを一、二枚ほどき、
春風が戸口に乞いに来ても、失ったとは感じない花。
passages.ko:
젊은 날의 내 삶은 꽃 같았다—풍성함 속에서 꽃잎 한둘을 놓아 주고,
봄바람이 문 앞에 구하러 와도 잃었다고 느끼지 않는 꽃.
passages.es:
Mi vida joven era como una flor que soltaba uno o dos pétalos de su abundancia
y no sentía pérdida cuando la brisa primaveral mendigaba a su puerta.
passages.fr:
Ma jeune vie était comme une fleur qui détache un ou deux pétales de son abondance
sans sentir de perte quand la brise printanière vient mendier à sa porte.
passages.de:
Mein junges Leben war wie eine Blume, die aus ihrer Fülle ein oder zwei Blätter löst
und keinen Verlust spürt, wenn der Frühlingswind an ihrer Tür bittet.
passages.it:
La mia giovane vita era come un fiore che lascia andare uno o due petali dalla sua abbondanza
senza sentire perdita quando la brezza di primavera bussa alla porta.
passages.pt:
Minha vida jovem era como uma flor que soltava uma ou duas pétalas de sua abundância
e não sentia perda quando a brisa da primavera vinha pedir à sua porta.
passages.ru:
Моя юная жизнь была как цветок, роняющий лепесток-другой из своего изобилия
и не знающий утраты, когда весенний ветер просит у двери.
passages.sv:
Mitt unga liv var som en blomma som släpper ett par kronblad ur sitt överflöd
och inte känner någon förlust när vårvinden ber vid dess dörr.
passages.ar:
كانت حياتي في الشباب كزهرة تُسقط بتلة أو اثنتين من وفرتها،
ولا تشعر بخسارة حين يأتي نسيم الربيع سائلاً عند بابها.
passages.hi:
यौवन में मेरा जीवन उस फूल सा था जो अपनी भरपूरता से एक-दो पंखुड़ियाँ छोड़ देता है,
और द्वार पर माँगने आई वसंत-बयार से कोई कमी नहीं महसूस करता।
passages.bn:
যৌবনে আমার জীবন ছিল ফুলের মতো—প্রাচুর্য থেকে এক-দুটি পাপড়ি ঝরিয়ে,
বসন্তের হাওয়া দুয়ারে চাইতে এলে কোনো ক্ষতি অনুভব করত না।
passages.id:
Hidupku ketika muda bagai bunga yang melepas satu dua kelopak dari kelimpahannya
dan tak merasa kehilangan saat angin musim semi meminta di pintunya.
passages.tr:
Gençliğimde hayatım, bolluğundan bir iki yaprak bırakan bir çiçek gibiydi;
bahar yeli kapısına dilenmeye gelince hiçbir eksiklik duymazdı.
passages.vi:
Đời tôi thuở trẻ như đóa hoa buông một hai cánh từ sự đầy tràn
mà chẳng thấy mất mát khi gió xuân đến xin bên cửa.
passages.th:
ชีวิตวัยเยาว์ของฉันเหมือนดอกไม้ที่ปล่อยกลีบหนึ่งสองกลีบจากความอุดม
และไม่รู้สึกสูญเสียเมื่อสายลมฤดูใบไม้ผลิมาขอที่ประตู

entries.passageOriginal:
Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and not also for withered leaves and faded flowers?
Is the song of the sea in tune only with the rising waves?
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: two questions challenge the idea that beauty and music belong only to beginnings, freshness, or rising motion.

passages.en:
Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and not also for withered leaves and faded flowers?
Is the song of the sea in tune only with the rising waves?
passages.zh-Hans:
夏日的节庆只属于新花，而不属于枯叶与残英吗？
海的歌声只与涌起的波浪合拍吗？
passages.zh-Hant:
夏日的節慶只屬於新花，而不屬於枯葉與殘英嗎？
海的歌聲只與湧起的波浪合拍嗎？
passages.ja:
夏の祭りは新しい花だけのもの、枯葉や色あせた花のものではないのか。
海の歌は立ち上がる波だけと調べを合わせるのか。
passages.ko:
여름의 축제는 새 꽃만을 위한 것이고 시든 잎과 바랜 꽃을 위한 것은 아닌가?
바다의 노래는 솟는 파도에만 가락을 맞추는가?
passages.es:
¿Es la fiesta del verano sólo para flores nuevas y no para hojas secas y flores marchitas?
¿Canta el mar sólo al compás de las olas que suben?
passages.fr:
La fête de l'été n'est-elle que pour les fleurs fraîches, non pour les feuilles sèches et les fleurs fanées ?
Le chant de la mer ne s'accorde-t-il qu'aux vagues montantes ?
passages.de:
Gilt das Fest des Sommers nur frischen Blüten, nicht auch welken Blättern und verblassten Blumen?
Stimmt das Lied des Meeres nur mit steigenden Wellen überein?
passages.it:
La festa d'estate è solo per i fiori freschi e non anche per foglie e fiori appassiti?
Il canto del mare si accorda soltanto alle onde che salgono?
passages.pt:
A festa do verão é só para flores novas, e não também para folhas e flores murchas?
A canção do mar acompanha apenas as ondas que sobem?
passages.ru:
Неужели праздник лета лишь для свежих цветов, а не для увядших листьев и поблёкших цветов?
Неужели песня моря созвучна лишь поднимающимся волнам?
passages.sv:
Är sommarens fest bara för nya blommor, inte också för vissna löv och blekta blommor?
Är havets sång endast i samklang med stigande vågor?
passages.ar:
هل مهرجان الصيف للأزهار النضرة وحدها، لا للأوراق الذابلة والزهور الباهتة أيضاً؟
وهل تنسجم أغنية البحر مع الأمواج الصاعدة وحدها؟
passages.hi:
क्या ग्रीष्म का उत्सव केवल नई कलियों के लिए है, सूखे पत्तों और मुरझाए फूलों के लिए नहीं?
क्या समुद्र का गीत केवल उठती लहरों से सुर मिलाता है?
passages.bn:
গ্রীষ্মের উৎসব কি শুধু নতুন ফুলের, শুকনো পাতা আর বিবর্ণ ফুলের নয়?
সমুদ্রের গান কি কেবল ওঠা ঢেউয়ের সঙ্গেই সুর মেলায়?
passages.id:
Apakah pesta musim panas hanya bagi bunga segar, bukan daun layu dan bunga pudar?
Apakah nyanyian laut hanya selaras dengan ombak yang naik?
passages.tr:
Yazın şöleni yalnız taze çiçekler için mi, solmuş yapraklarla çiçekler için değil mi?
Denizin şarkısı yalnız yükselen dalgalarla mı uyumlu?
passages.vi:
Lễ hội mùa hè chỉ dành cho hoa tươi, không dành cho lá úa và hoa tàn sao?
Khúc hát biển chỉ hòa điệu cùng những con sóng dâng sao?
passages.th:
เทศกาลฤดูร้อนมีไว้เพียงสำหรับดอกไม้สด มิใช่ใบเหี่ยวและดอกไม้โรยด้วยหรือ
เพลงของทะเลเข้าจังหวะเฉพาะกับคลื่นที่กำลังสูงขึ้นหรือ

entries.passageOriginal:
ON the seashore of endless worlds children meet.
The infinite sky is motionless overhead and the restless water is boisterous.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.originalWorkTitle: The Crescent Moon: On the Seashore
entries.englishWorkTitle: The Crescent Moon: On the Seashore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: children gather at a cosmic shoreline between a still infinite sky and loud, restless water.

passages.en:
ON the seashore of endless worlds children meet.
The infinite sky is motionless overhead and the restless water is boisterous.
passages.zh-Hans:
在无尽世界的海岸上，孩子们相聚。
无限的天空静止在头顶，不安的海水喧腾。
passages.zh-Hant:
在無盡世界的海岸上，孩子們相聚。
無限的天空靜止在頭頂，不安的海水喧騰。
passages.ja:
果てしない世界の浜辺で、子どもたちは出会う。
頭上の無限の空は静まり、落ち着かぬ水は騒いでいる。
passages.ko:
끝없는 세계의 바닷가에서 아이들이 만난다.
머리 위 무한한 하늘은 고요하고 쉬지 않는 물은 떠들썩하다.
passages.es:
En la orilla de mundos sin fin se reúnen los niños.
El cielo infinito está inmóvil y el agua inquieta alborota.
passages.fr:
Sur le rivage des mondes sans fin, les enfants se rencontrent.
Le ciel infini demeure immobile et l'eau inquiète gronde.
passages.de:
Am Ufer endloser Welten treffen sich die Kinder.
Der unendliche Himmel steht still, und das ruhelose Wasser lärmt.
passages.it:
Sulla riva di mondi infiniti s'incontrano i bambini.
Il cielo infinito è immobile e l'acqua inquieta rumoreggia.
passages.pt:
Na praia de mundos sem fim, as crianças se encontram.
O céu infinito fica imóvel, e a água inquieta faz alarido.
passages.ru:
На берегу бесконечных миров встречаются дети.
Безграничное небо недвижно, а беспокойная вода шумит.
passages.sv:
På stranden till ändlösa världar möts barnen.
Den oändliga himlen står still och det rastlösa vattnet brusar.
passages.ar:
على شاطئ العوالم التي لا تنتهي يلتقي الأطفال.
السماء اللانهائية ساكنة فوقهم والماء القلق صاخب.
passages.hi:
अनंत संसारों के समुद्र-तट पर बच्चे मिलते हैं।
ऊपर असीम आकाश निश्चल है और बेचैन जल कोलाहल करता है।
passages.bn:
অন্তহীন জগতের সমুদ্রতীরে শিশুরা মেলে।
মাথার ওপর অসীম আকাশ স্থির, অশান্ত জল কলরবময়।
passages.id:
Di pantai dunia-dunia tanpa akhir, anak-anak bertemu.
Langit tak berhingga diam di atas dan air yang gelisah bergemuruh.
passages.tr:
Sonsuz dünyaların kıyısında çocuklar buluşur.
Başlarındaki sonsuz gök durgun, huzursuz su gürültülüdür.
passages.vi:
Trên bờ biển của những thế giới vô tận, trẻ thơ gặp nhau.
Bầu trời vô biên bất động trên cao, còn nước không yên thì náo động.
passages.th:
บนชายฝั่งแห่งโลกอันไม่สิ้นสุด เด็ก ๆ มาพบกัน
ท้องฟ้าไร้ขอบเขตนิ่งอยู่เหนือศีรษะ ส่วนน้ำที่ไม่สงบส่งเสียงครืนครั่น

entries.passageOriginal:
I shall become a delicate draught of air and caress you;
and I shall be ripples in the water when you bathe, and kiss you and kiss you again.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: a child imagines remaining close to the mother after death by returning as air and water.

passages.en:
I shall become a delicate draught of air and caress you;
and I shall be ripples in the water when you bathe, and kiss you and kiss you again.
passages.zh-Hans:
我将化作一缕轻柔的风抚摸你；
你沐浴时，我将成为水波，一遍又一遍地吻你。
passages.zh-Hant:
我將化作一縷輕柔的風撫摸你；
你沐浴時，我將成為水波，一遍又一遍地吻你。
passages.ja:
私はやさしい風になってあなたを撫でよう。
あなたが水浴びするとき水の波紋になり、何度も口づけよう。
passages.ko:
나는 부드러운 한 줄기 바람이 되어 당신을 어루만지고,
당신이 씻을 때 물결이 되어 거듭 입맞추리라.
passages.es:
Me volveré una brisa delicada y te acariciaré;
y seré ondas en el agua cuando te bañes, y te besaré una y otra vez.
passages.fr:
Je deviendrai un souffle délicat et te caresserai ;
je serai les rides de l'eau quand tu te baigneras, et je t'embrasserai encore.
passages.de:
Ich werde ein zarter Luftzug und dich liebkosen;
beim Baden werde ich Wellen im Wasser sein und dich immer wieder küssen.
passages.it:
Diventerò un soffio delicato e ti accarezzerò;
e sarò increspature nell'acqua quando ti bagni, baciandoti ancora e ancora.
passages.pt:
Serei uma brisa delicada e te acariciarei;
e serei ondas na água quando te banhares, beijando-te vezes sem fim.
passages.ru:
Я стану нежным дуновением и приласкаю тебя;
стану рябью в воде, когда ты купаешься, и буду целовать тебя вновь и вновь.
passages.sv:
Jag ska bli en mild vindfläkt och smeka dig;
och bli krusningar i vattnet när du badar och kyssa dig om och om igen.
passages.ar:
سأصير نسمة رقيقة تداعبك؛
وسأكون تموجات الماء حين تستحم، وأقبلك مرة بعد مرة.
passages.hi:
मैं हवा का कोमल झोंका बनकर तुम्हें सहलाऊँगा;
और तुम्हारे नहाते समय जल की लहर बनकर बार-बार तुम्हें चूमूँगा।
passages.bn:
আমি কোমল বাতাস হয়ে তোমায় আদর করব;
তুমি স্নান করলে জলের ঢেউ হয়ে বারবার চুমু দেব।
passages.id:
Aku akan menjadi embusan lembut dan membelaimu;
dan menjadi riak saat kau mandi, menciummu lagi dan lagi.
passages.tr:
Narin bir esinti olup seni okşayacağım;
yıkandığında suda halkalar olup seni tekrar tekrar öpeceğim.
passages.vi:
Tôi sẽ hóa thành làn gió nhẹ vuốt ve người;
và thành gợn nước khi người tắm, hôn người hết lần này đến lần khác.
passages.th:
ฉันจะกลายเป็นสายลมอ่อนโยนและลูบไล้เธอ
เมื่อเธออาบน้ำ ฉันจะเป็นระลอกน้ำและจุมพิตเธอครั้งแล้วครั้งเล่า

entries.passageOriginal:
Life as a whole never takes death seriously.
It laughs, dances and plays, it builds, hoards and loves in death's face.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English prose: he distinguishes life's continuing creative activity from an individual's fear of death.

passages.en:
Life as a whole never takes death seriously.
It laughs, dances and plays, it builds, hoards and loves in death's face.
passages.zh-Hans:
生命作为一个整体，从不把死亡看得过于严肃。
它面对死亡仍欢笑、舞蹈、游戏，仍建造、积聚并爱。
passages.zh-Hant:
生命作為一個整體，從不把死亡看得過於嚴肅。
它面對死亡仍歡笑、舞蹈、遊戲，仍建造、積聚並愛。
passages.ja:
生命全体は、死を深刻に受け取りはしない。
死を前にしても笑い、踊り、遊び、築き、蓄え、愛する。
passages.ko:
전체로서의 생명은 죽음을 심각하게 여기지 않는다.
죽음 앞에서도 웃고 춤추고 놀며, 짓고 모으고 사랑한다.
passages.es:
La vida entera nunca se toma en serio la muerte.
Ríe, baila y juega; construye, guarda y ama frente a la muerte.
passages.fr:
La vie dans son ensemble ne prend jamais la mort au sérieux.
Elle rit, danse et joue ; elle bâtit, amasse et aime face à la mort.
passages.de:
Das Leben als Ganzes nimmt den Tod nie ernst.
Es lacht, tanzt und spielt, baut, sammelt und liebt dem Tod ins Gesicht.
passages.it:
La vita nel suo insieme non prende mai sul serio la morte.
Ride, danza e gioca; costruisce, accumula e ama di fronte alla morte.
passages.pt:
A vida inteira nunca leva a morte a sério.
Ela ri, dança e brinca; constrói, guarda e ama diante da morte.
passages.ru:
Жизнь в целом никогда не принимает смерть всерьёз.
Перед лицом смерти она смеётся, танцует, играет, строит, копит и любит.
passages.sv:
Livet som helhet tar aldrig döden på allvar.
Det skrattar, dansar och leker, bygger, samlar och älskar inför döden.
passages.ar:
الحياة في كليتها لا تأخذ الموت على محمل الجد.
تضحك وترقص وتلعب، وتبني وتدّخر وتحب في وجه الموت.
passages.hi:
समग्र जीवन मृत्यु को कभी गंभीरता से नहीं लेता।
वह मृत्यु के सामने हँसता, नाचता, खेलता, बनाता, सँजोता और प्रेम करता है।
passages.bn:
সমগ্র জীবন মৃত্যুকে কখনও গুরুতর করে দেখে না।
মৃত্যুর মুখে সে হাসে, নাচে, খেলে, গড়ে, সঞ্চয় করে ও ভালোবাসে।
passages.id:
Kehidupan sebagai keseluruhan tak pernah menganggap maut terlalu serius.
Ia tertawa, menari, bermain, membangun, menyimpan, dan mencinta di hadapan maut.
passages.tr:
Bir bütün olarak hayat ölümü hiç ciddiye almaz.
Ölümün yüzüne karşı güler, dans eder, oynar, kurar, biriktirir ve sever.
passages.vi:
Sự sống như một toàn thể không bao giờ quá coi trọng cái chết.
Trước mặt cái chết, nó vẫn cười, múa, chơi, xây dựng, vun góp và yêu.
passages.th:
ชีวิตโดยรวมไม่เคยถือความตายเป็นเรื่องใหญ่
ต่อหน้าความตาย มันยังหัวเราะ เต้นรำ เล่น สร้าง สะสม และรัก

entries.passageOriginal:
The meaning of the living words that come out of the experiences of great hearts
can never be exhausted by any one system of logical interpretation.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English prose: the preface argues that language born of lived experience cannot be contained by a single explanatory system.

passages.en:
The meaning of the living words that come out of the experiences of great hearts
can never be exhausted by any one system of logical interpretation.
passages.zh-Hans:
从伟大心灵的经验中生出的鲜活言语，
其意义绝不会被任何一种逻辑解释体系穷尽。
passages.zh-Hant:
從偉大心靈的經驗中生出的鮮活言語，
其意義絕不會被任何一種邏輯解釋體系窮盡。
passages.ja:
偉大な心の経験から生まれる、生きた言葉の意味は、
ただ一つの論理解釈の体系によって尽くされることはない。
passages.ko:
위대한 마음의 경험에서 나온 살아 있는 말의 뜻은
어느 하나의 논리적 해석 체계로도 결코 다 헤아릴 수 없다.
passages.es:
El sentido de las palabras vivas nacidas de la experiencia de grandes corazones
jamás se agota en un solo sistema de interpretación lógica.
passages.fr:
Le sens des paroles vivantes issues de l'expérience des grands cœurs
ne peut jamais être épuisé par un seul système d'interprétation logique.
passages.de:
Der Sinn lebendiger Worte aus den Erfahrungen großer Herzen
kann durch kein einziges System logischer Deutung ausgeschöpft werden.
passages.it:
Il senso delle parole vive nate dall'esperienza di grandi cuori
non può mai esaurirsi in un solo sistema d'interpretazione logica.
passages.pt:
O sentido das palavras vivas que nascem da experiência de grandes corações
jamais se esgota num único sistema de interpretação lógica.
passages.ru:
Смысл живых слов, рождённых опытом великих сердец,
никогда не исчерпать одной системой логического толкования.
passages.sv:
Betydelsen i levande ord som föds ur stora hjärtans erfarenheter
kan aldrig uttömmas av ett enda logiskt tolkningssystem.
passages.ar:
معنى الكلمات الحية الخارجة من تجارب القلوب العظيمة
لا يمكن أن يستنفده نظام واحد من التفسير المنطقي.
passages.hi:
महान हृदयों के अनुभव से निकले जीवित शब्दों का अर्थ
तर्कपूर्ण व्याख्या की किसी एक प्रणाली से कभी समाप्त नहीं होता।
passages.bn:
মহৎ হৃদয়ের অভিজ্ঞতা থেকে আসা জীবন্ত কথার অর্থ
কোনো একটি যুক্তিনির্ভর ব্যাখ্যা দিয়ে কখনও নিঃশেষ হয় না।
passages.id:
Makna kata-kata hidup yang lahir dari pengalaman hati besar
tak pernah habis oleh satu sistem tafsir logis.
passages.tr:
Büyük yüreklerin deneyimlerinden doğan canlı sözlerin anlamı
hiçbir tek mantıksal yorum sistemiyle tüketilemez.
passages.vi:
Ý nghĩa của những lời sống động sinh ra từ trải nghiệm của những trái tim lớn
không bao giờ cạn trong một hệ thống diễn giải logic duy nhất.
passages.th:
ความหมายของถ้อยคำมีชีวิตซึ่งเกิดจากประสบการณ์ของหัวใจอันยิ่งใหญ่
ไม่มีวันถูกอธิบายจนหมดด้วยระบบตรรกะเพียงระบบเดียว

entries.passageOriginal:
In love we find a joy which is ultimate
because it is the ultimate truth.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.originalWorkTitle: Creative Unity: An Indian Folk Religion
entries.englishWorkTitle: Creative Unity: An Indian Folk Religion
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English prose: in an essay on the Bauls of Bengal, he connects love's joy with a truth felt as final rather than provisional.

passages.en:
In love we find a joy which is ultimate
because it is the ultimate truth.
passages.zh-Hans:
在爱中，我们找到一种终极的喜悦，
因为爱是终极的真实。
passages.zh-Hant:
在愛中，我們找到一種終極的喜悅，
因為愛是終極的真實。
passages.ja:
愛の中に、私たちは究極の喜びを見いだす。
それが究極の真実だから。
passages.ko:
사랑 안에서 우리는 궁극의 기쁨을 찾는다.
사랑이 궁극의 진실이기 때문이다.
passages.es:
En el amor hallamos una alegría última,
porque es la verdad última.
passages.fr:
Dans l'amour nous trouvons une joie ultime,
parce qu'il est la vérité ultime.
passages.de:
In der Liebe finden wir höchste Freude,
weil sie die höchste Wahrheit ist.
passages.it:
Nell'amore troviamo una gioia ultima,
perché è la verità ultima.
passages.pt:
No amor encontramos uma alegria última,
porque ele é a verdade última.
passages.ru:
В любви мы находим высшую радость,
потому что она — высшая истина.
passages.sv:
I kärleken finner vi den yttersta glädjen,
eftersom den är den yttersta sanningen.
passages.ar:
في الحب نجد فرحاً نهائياً،
لأنه الحقيقة النهائية.
passages.hi:
प्रेम में हमें परम आनंद मिलता है,
क्योंकि वही परम सत्य है।
passages.bn:
ভালোবাসায় আমরা চরম আনন্দ পাই,
কারণ সেটিই চরম সত্য।
passages.id:
Dalam cinta kita menemukan sukacita tertinggi,
karena cinta adalah kebenaran tertinggi.
passages.tr:
Sevgide nihai bir sevinç buluruz,
çünkü o nihai gerçektir.
passages.vi:
Trong tình yêu ta tìm thấy niềm vui tận cùng,
bởi đó là chân lý tận cùng.
passages.th:
ในความรัก เราพบความยินดีสูงสุด
เพราะมันคือความจริงสูงสุด

entries.passageOriginal:
Perfection of unity is not in uniformity,
but in harmony.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English prose: he distinguishes living unity, which preserves real differences, from a merely imposed sameness.

passages.en:
Perfection of unity is not in uniformity,
but in harmony.
passages.zh-Hans:
统一的圆满不在于整齐划一，
而在于和谐。
passages.zh-Hant:
統一的圓滿不在於整齊劃一，
而在於和諧。
passages.ja:
一体性の完成は画一性にあるのではなく、
調和にある。
passages.ko:
하나됨의 완성은 획일성에 있지 않고,
조화에 있다.
passages.es:
La perfección de la unidad no está en la uniformidad,
sino en la armonía.
passages.fr:
La perfection de l'unité n'est pas dans l'uniformité,
mais dans l'harmonie.
passages.de:
Die Vollkommenheit der Einheit liegt nicht in Gleichförmigkeit,
sondern in Harmonie.
passages.it:
La perfezione dell'unità non è nell'uniformità,
ma nell'armonia.
passages.pt:
A perfeição da unidade não está na uniformidade,
mas na harmonia.
passages.ru:
Совершенство единства не в единообразии,
а в гармонии.
passages.sv:
Enhetens fulländning finns inte i likformighet,
utan i harmoni.
passages.ar:
كمال الوحدة ليس في التماثل،
بل في الانسجام.
passages.hi:
एकता की पूर्णता एकरूपता में नहीं,
बल्कि सामंजस्य में है।
passages.bn:
ঐক্যের পূর্ণতা একরূপতায় নয়,
সামঞ্জস্যে।
passages.id:
Kesempurnaan kesatuan bukanlah dalam keseragaman,
melainkan dalam keselarasan.
passages.tr:
Birliğin kusursuzluğu tekbiçimlilikte değil,
uyumdadır.
passages.vi:
Sự hoàn hảo của thống nhất không nằm ở đồng dạng,
mà ở hòa hợp.
passages.th:
ความสมบูรณ์ของความเป็นหนึ่งไม่ได้อยู่ที่ความเหมือนกันทั้งหมด
แต่อยู่ที่ความกลมกลืน

entries.passageOriginal:
Give me the supreme courage of love, this is my prayer—
the courage to speak, to do, to suffer at thy will, to leave all things or be left alone.
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.englishContextNote: From Tagore's own published English version: the prayer asks for a love strong enough to act, endure, release possessions, and withstand solitude.

passages.en:
Give me the supreme courage of love, this is my prayer—
the courage to speak, to do, to suffer at thy will, to leave all things or be left alone.
passages.zh-Hans:
请赐我爱的至高勇气，这是我的祈求——
敢于言说、行动、承受，敢于放下一切，或独自留下。
passages.zh-Hant:
請賜我愛的至高勇氣，這是我的祈求——
敢於言說、行動、承受，敢於放下一切，或獨自留下。
passages.ja:
愛の至高の勇気を与えたまえ、これが私の祈り——
語り、行い、耐え、すべてを手放し、あるいは独り残る勇気を。
passages.ko:
사랑의 지극한 용기를 주소서, 이것이 나의 기도—
말하고 행하고 견디며, 모든 것을 떠나거나 홀로 남을 용기를.
passages.es:
Dame el valor supremo del amor, ésta es mi plegaria: 
el valor de hablar, actuar, sufrir, dejarlo todo o quedar solo.
passages.fr:
Donne-moi le courage suprême de l'amour, telle est ma prière :
le courage de parler, d'agir, de souffrir, de tout quitter ou de rester seul.
passages.de:
Gib mir den höchsten Mut der Liebe, darum bete ich: 
den Mut zu sprechen, zu handeln, zu leiden, alles zu verlassen oder allein zu bleiben.
passages.it:
Dammi il coraggio supremo dell'amore, questa è la mia preghiera: 
il coraggio di parlare, agire, soffrire, lasciare tutto o restare solo.
passages.pt:
Dá-me a coragem suprema do amor, esta é minha prece: 
a coragem de falar, agir, sofrer, deixar tudo ou ficar só.
passages.ru:
Дай мне высшее мужество любви — вот моя молитва: 
мужество говорить, действовать, страдать, оставить всё или остаться одному.
passages.sv:
Ge mig kärlekens högsta mod, detta är min bön: 
mod att tala, handla, lida, lämna allt eller bli lämnad ensam.
passages.ar:
امنحني شجاعة الحب القصوى، هذه صلاتي—
شجاعة الكلام والفعل والاحتمال، وترك كل شيء أو البقاء وحيداً.
passages.hi:
मुझे प्रेम का सर्वोच्च साहस दो—यही मेरी प्रार्थना है—
बोलने, करने, सहने, सब छोड़ने या अकेले रह जाने का साहस।
passages.bn:
আমায় ভালোবাসার পরম সাহস দাও—এই আমার প্রার্থনা—
বলার, করার, সহ্য করার, সব ছাড়ার কিংবা একা থাকার সাহস।
passages.id:
Berilah aku keberanian tertinggi dari cinta, inilah doaku—
keberanian berbicara, bertindak, menderita, meninggalkan segalanya atau tinggal sendiri.
passages.tr:
Bana sevginin yüce cesaretini ver, duam budur—
konuşma, yapma, dayanma, her şeyi bırakma ya da yalnız kalma cesaretini.
passages.vi:
Xin cho tôi lòng can đảm tối cao của tình yêu—đó là lời nguyện—
dám nói, làm, chịu đựng, rời bỏ tất cả hoặc ở lại một mình.
passages.th:
โปรดประทานความกล้าสูงสุดแห่งความรัก นี่คือคำอธิษฐานของฉัน—
กล้าที่จะพูด ทำ อดทน ละทิ้งทุกสิ่ง หรืออยู่ลำพัง

entries.passageOriginal:
Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen,
die sich über die Dinge ziehn.
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.originalWorkTitle: Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen
entries.englishWorkTitle: I Live My Life in Widening Rings
entries.englishContextNote: The self is imagined as a continuing circular movement whose reach grows beyond the things immediately known.

passages.en:
I live my life in widening rings
that stretch themselves over all things.
passages.zh-Hans:
我生活在不断扩展的圆环中，
它们延伸越过万物。
passages.zh-Hant:
我生活在不斷擴展的圓環中，
它們延伸越過萬物。
passages.ja:
私は広がりゆく輪の中で人生を生きる、
その輪はあらゆるものの上へ伸びてゆく。
passages.ko:
나는 넓어져 가는 원들 속에서 삶을 산다,
그 원들은 모든 것 위로 뻗어 간다.
passages.es:
Vivo mi vida en círculos crecientes
que se extienden sobre las cosas.
passages.fr:
Je vis ma vie en cercles grandissants
qui s’étendent par-dessus les choses.
passages.de:
Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen,
die sich über die Dinge ziehn.
passages.it:
Vivo la mia vita in cerchi crescenti
che si stendono sopra le cose.
passages.pt:
Vivo minha vida em círculos crescentes
que se estendem sobre as coisas.
passages.ru:
Я живу свою жизнь в растущих кругах,
что расходятся поверх вещей.
passages.sv:
Jag lever mitt liv i växande ringar
som sträcker sig över tingen.
passages.ar:
أعيش حياتي في دوائر تتسع،
وتمتد فوق الأشياء.
passages.hi:
मैं अपना जीवन बढ़ते हुए वृत्तों में जीता हूँ,
जो वस्तुओं के ऊपर फैलते जाते हैं।
passages.bn:
আমি আমার জীবন কাটাই ক্রমবর্ধমান বৃত্তে,
যেগুলো সব কিছুর ওপর ছড়িয়ে যায়।
passages.id:
Aku menjalani hidup dalam lingkaran yang melebar,
yang membentang melampaui segala benda.
passages.tr:
Hayatımı genişleyen halkalarda yaşarım,
eşyaların üzerine yayılırlar.
passages.vi:
Tôi sống đời mình trong những vòng tròn rộng dần,
chúng trải ra trên vạn vật.
passages.th:
ฉันใช้ชีวิตในวงแหวนที่กว้างขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ
ซึ่งทอดผ่านเหนือสรรพสิ่ง

entries.passageOriginal:
Wer du auch seist: am Abend tritt hinaus
aus deiner Stube, drin du alles weißt;
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: The poem opens by asking an unnamed reader to leave the room of familiar knowledge and step into evening.

passages.en:
Whoever you may be: step out at evening
from your room, where you know everything;
passages.zh-Hans:
无论你是谁：傍晚时走出去，
离开那间你熟知一切的屋子；
passages.zh-Hant:
無論你是誰：傍晚時走出去，
離開那間你熟知一切的屋子；
passages.ja:
あなたが誰であれ、夕暮れに外へ出よ、
すべてを知っているその部屋から。
passages.ko:
당신이 누구든, 저녁이면 밖으로 나가라,
모든 것을 안다고 여기는 방에서.
passages.es:
Quienquiera que seas: sal al atardecer
de tu cuarto, donde todo lo sabes;
passages.fr:
Qui que tu sois : sors au soir
de ta chambre où tu sais tout ;
passages.de:
Wer du auch seist: am Abend tritt hinaus
aus deiner Stube, drin du alles weißt;
passages.it:
Chiunque tu sia: esci la sera
dalla tua stanza, dove sai ogni cosa;
passages.pt:
Quem quer que sejas: sai ao entardecer
do teu quarto, onde sabes tudo;
passages.ru:
Кем бы ты ни был: вечером выйди
из комнаты, где тебе всё известно;
passages.sv:
Vem du än är: gå ut om kvällen
ur ditt rum, där du vet allt;
passages.ar:
أياً تكن: اخرج عند المساء
من غرفتك التي تعرف فيها كل شيء؛
passages.hi:
तुम जो भी हो: संध्या में बाहर निकलो
अपने उस कमरे से, जहाँ तुम सब कुछ जानते हो;
passages.bn:
তুমি যে-ই হও: সন্ধ্যায় বেরিয়ে এসো
তোমার সেই ঘর থেকে, যেখানে সব জানো;
passages.id:
Siapa pun dirimu: keluarlah saat petang
dari kamarmu, tempat kau mengetahui segalanya;
passages.tr:
Kim olursan ol: akşam dışarı çık
her şeyi bildiğin odandan;
passages.vi:
Dù bạn là ai: hãy bước ra lúc chiều xuống
khỏi căn phòng nơi bạn biết mọi điều;
passages.th:
ไม่ว่าเธอเป็นใคร จงก้าวออกไปยามเย็น
จากห้องที่เธอรู้ทุกสิ่ง

entries.passageOriginal:
Und wieder rauscht mein tiefes Leben lauter,
als ob es jetzt in breitern Ufern ginge.
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: Inner development is heard as a deep current becoming louder because its banks have widened.

passages.en:
And once again my deep life rushes louder,
as though it now flowed between wider banks.
passages.zh-Hans:
我深处的生命再次响得更洪亮，
仿佛此刻正流过更宽阔的河岸。
passages.zh-Hant:
我深處的生命再次響得更洪亮，
彷彿此刻正流過更寬闊的河岸。
passages.ja:
そして再び、私の深い生はより高く響く、
今や広い岸のあいだを流れるかのように。
passages.ko:
그리고 다시 내 깊은 삶이 더 크게 흐른다,
이제 더 넓은 강둑 사이를 가는 듯이.
passages.es:
Y de nuevo mi vida profunda suena más fuerte,
como si ahora corriera entre orillas más anchas.
passages.fr:
Et de nouveau ma vie profonde bruit plus fort,
comme si elle coulait entre des rives plus larges.
passages.de:
Und wieder rauscht mein tiefes Leben lauter,
als ob es jetzt in breitern Ufern ginge.
passages.it:
E di nuovo la mia vita profonda scorre più sonora,
come se ora passasse tra rive più ampie.
passages.pt:
E novamente minha vida profunda soa mais forte,
como se agora corresse entre margens mais largas.
passages.ru:
И вновь моя глубокая жизнь шумит громче,
словно теперь течёт между более широких берегов.
passages.sv:
Och åter brusar mitt djupa liv högre,
som om det nu flöt mellan bredare stränder.
passages.ar:
ومن جديد تهدر حياتي العميقة أعلى،
كأنها تجري الآن بين ضفاف أوسع.
passages.hi:
और फिर मेरा गहरा जीवन अधिक ऊँचा बहता है,
मानो अब वह चौड़े तटों के बीच चल रहा हो।
passages.bn:
আবার আমার গভীর জীবন আরও জোরে বয়ে যায়,
যেন এখন তা আরও প্রশস্ত তীরের মাঝে চলছে।
passages.id:
Dan sekali lagi hidupku yang dalam menderu lebih keras,
seolah kini mengalir di antara tebing yang lebih lebar.
passages.tr:
Ve derin hayatım yeniden daha gür çağlıyor,
sanki artık daha geniş kıyılar arasında akıyor.
passages.vi:
Và một lần nữa đời sâu thẳm trong tôi vang lớn hơn,
như thể giờ chảy giữa đôi bờ rộng hơn.
passages.th:
และอีกครั้ง ชีวิตส่วนลึกของฉันไหลก้องดังขึ้น
ราวกับบัดนี้ไหลอยู่ระหว่างฝั่งที่กว้างกว่าเดิม

entries.passageOriginal:
Herr: es ist Zeit. Der Sommer war sehr groß.
Leg Deinen Schatten auf die Sonnenuhren
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: At the seasonal turning point, the speaker acknowledges summer’s fullness and calls for autumn’s shadow.

passages.en:
Lord: it is time. The summer was immense.
Lay your shadow upon the sundials
passages.zh-Hans:
主啊：时候到了。夏日曾如此浩大。
把你的影子放在日晷上
passages.zh-Hant:
主啊：時候到了。夏日曾如此浩大。
把你的影子放在日晷上
passages.ja:
主よ、時です。夏はとても大きかった。
日時計の上にあなたの影を置いてください
passages.ko:
주여, 때가 되었습니다. 여름은 참으로 거대했습니다.
해시계 위에 당신의 그림자를 드리우소서
passages.es:
Señor: es hora. El verano fue inmenso.
Pon tu sombra sobre los relojes de sol
passages.fr:
Seigneur : il est temps. L’été fut immense.
Pose ton ombre sur les cadrans solaires
passages.de:
Herr: es ist Zeit. Der Sommer war sehr groß.
Leg Deinen Schatten auf die Sonnenuhren
passages.it:
Signore: è tempo. L’estate fu immensa.
Posa la tua ombra sulle meridiane
passages.pt:
Senhor: é tempo. O verão foi imenso.
Põe tua sombra sobre os relógios de sol
passages.ru:
Господи: пора. Велико было лето.
Положи свою тень на солнечные часы
passages.sv:
Herre: det är tid. Sommaren var väldig.
Lägg din skugga över soluren
passages.ar:
يا رب: حان الوقت. كان الصيف عظيماً.
ألقِ ظلك على الساعات الشمسية
passages.hi:
प्रभु: समय आ गया। ग्रीष्म बहुत विशाल था।
धूपघड़ियों पर अपनी छाया रख दो
passages.bn:
প্রভু: সময় হয়েছে। গ্রীষ্ম ছিল বিপুল।
সূর্যঘড়িগুলোর ওপর তোমার ছায়া রাখো
passages.id:
Tuhan: telah tiba waktunya. Musim panas begitu luas.
Letakkan bayang-Mu di atas jam matahari
passages.tr:
Tanrım: vakit geldi. Yaz çok büyüktü.
Gölgeliğini güneş saatlerinin üzerine bırak
passages.vi:
Lạy Chúa: đã đến lúc. Mùa hè thật lớn lao.
Hãy đặt bóng Người lên những đồng hồ mặt trời
passages.th:
พระผู้เป็นเจ้า ถึงเวลาแล้ว ฤดูร้อนช่างยิ่งใหญ่
โปรดทอดเงาของพระองค์ลงบนแดดนาฬิกา

entries.passageOriginal:
Und doch ist Einer welcher dieses Fallen
unendlich sanft in seinen Händen hält.
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: After leaves, earth, and human hands are pictured falling, the poem closes with an image of that falling being held.

passages.en:
And yet there is One who holds this falling
infinitely gently in his hands.
passages.zh-Hans:
然而有一位把这一切坠落
无限温柔地托在手中。
passages.zh-Hant:
然而有一位把這一切墜落
無限溫柔地托在手中。
passages.ja:
それでも、この落下を
限りなく優しく手に受ける者がいる。
passages.ko:
그럼에도 이 모든 낙하를
한없이 부드럽게 손에 받드는 이가 있다.
passages.es:
Y, sin embargo, hay Uno que sostiene esta caída
con infinita ternura entre sus manos.
passages.fr:
Et pourtant il en est Un qui tient cette chute
infiniment doucement dans ses mains.
passages.de:
Und doch ist Einer welcher dieses Fallen
unendlich sanft in seinen Händen hält.
passages.it:
Eppure c’è Uno che regge questa caduta
con infinita dolcezza nelle sue mani.
passages.pt:
E no entanto há Um que sustém essa queda
infinitamente suave em suas mãos.
passages.ru:
И всё же есть Тот, кто это падение
бесконечно нежно держит в своих руках.
passages.sv:
Och ändå finns En som håller detta fall
oändligt varsamt i sina händer.
passages.ar:
ومع ذلك هناك من يحمل هذا السقوط
برفق لا نهاية له بين يديه.
passages.hi:
फिर भी कोई है जो इस गिरने को
अपने हाथों में अनंत कोमलता से थामे है।
passages.bn:
তবু একজন আছেন যিনি এই পতনকে
নিজ হাতে অসীম কোমলতায় ধরে রাখেন।
passages.id:
Namun ada Seseorang yang menahan kejatuhan ini
dengan kelembutan tak terbatas di tangannya.
passages.tr:
Yine de bu düşüşü
ellerinde sonsuz bir yumuşaklıkla tutan Biri var.
passages.vi:
Vậy mà có Một Người đỡ lấy sự rơi này
vô cùng dịu dàng trong đôi tay.
passages.th:
ถึงกระนั้น ยังมีผู้หนึ่งคอยรองรับการร่วงหล่นนี้
ไว้อย่างอ่อนโยนไร้สิ้นสุดในมือของเขา

entries.passageOriginal:
Sein Wachstum ist: der Tiefbesiegte
von immer Größerem zu sein.
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: The closing redefines growth not as domination but as yielding deeply to realities larger than oneself.

passages.en:
His growth is this: to be deeply overcome
by ever greater things.
passages.zh-Hans:
他的成长是：深深地被
愈来愈伟大的事物所征服。
passages.zh-Hant:
他的成長是：深深地被
愈來愈偉大的事物所征服。
passages.ja:
彼の成長とは、深く打ち負かされること、
ますます大いなるものによって。
passages.ko:
그의 성장은 이것이다. 깊이 패배하는 것,
점점 더 큰 것들에 의해.
passages.es:
Su crecimiento consiste en ser vencido profundamente
por cosas cada vez mayores.
passages.fr:
Sa croissance est d’être profondément vaincu
par des choses toujours plus grandes.
passages.de:
Sein Wachstum ist: der Tiefbesiegte
von immer Größerem zu sein.
passages.it:
La sua crescita è essere vinto nel profondo
da cose sempre più grandi.
passages.pt:
Seu crescimento é ser profundamente vencido
por coisas sempre maiores.
passages.ru:
Его рост — быть глубоко побеждённым
всё более великим.
passages.sv:
Hans växande är att bli djupt besegrad
av allt större ting.
passages.ar:
نموه هو أن يُغلب في أعماقه
بأشياء أعظم فأعظم.
passages.hi:
उसकी वृद्धि यह है: गहराई से पराजित होना
निरंतर बड़ी होती चीज़ों से।
passages.bn:
তার বেড়ে ওঠা হলো: গভীরভাবে পরাজিত হওয়া
ক্রমশ বৃহত্তর কিছুর কাছে।
passages.id:
Pertumbuhannya ialah ditaklukkan sedalam-dalamnya
oleh hal-hal yang semakin besar.
passages.tr:
Onun büyümesi, derinden yenilmektir
gittikçe daha büyük şeylerce.
passages.vi:
Sự trưởng thành của người ấy là bị khuất phục tận sâu
bởi những điều ngày một lớn lao hơn.
passages.th:
การเติบโตของเขาคือการพ่ายแพ้อย่างลึกซึ้ง
ต่อสิ่งที่ยิ่งใหญ่ขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ

entries.passageOriginal:
Der Abdruck meiner kleinsten Bewegung
bleibt in der seidenen Stille sichtbar;
entries.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
entries.englishContextNote: In separation from the beloved, silence becomes a sensitive surface on which even the smallest movement leaves a trace.

passages.en:
The imprint of my smallest movement
remains visible in the silken silence;
passages.zh-Hans:
我最微小动作的印痕
仍在丝绸般的寂静中清晰可见；
passages.zh-Hant:
我最微小動作的印痕
仍在絲綢般的寂靜中清晰可見；
passages.ja:
私の最も小さな動きの跡が
絹のような静けさの中に見えたまま残る。
passages.ko:
나의 가장 작은 움직임의 자국이
비단 같은 고요 속에 보이는 채 남는다.
passages.es:
La huella de mi más pequeño movimiento
permanece visible en el silencio de seda;
passages.fr:
L’empreinte de mon moindre mouvement
reste visible dans le silence de soie ;
passages.de:
Der Abdruck meiner kleinsten Bewegung
bleibt in der seidenen Stille sichtbar;
passages.it:
L’impronta del mio più piccolo movimento
resta visibile nel silenzio di seta;
passages.pt:
A marca do meu menor movimento
permanece visível no silêncio de seda;
passages.ru:
Отпечаток малейшего моего движения
остаётся видимым в шёлковой тишине;
passages.sv:
Avtrycket av min minsta rörelse
förblir synligt i den silkeslena tystnaden;
passages.ar:
يبقى أثر أصغر حركة مني
مرئياً في الصمت الحريري؛
passages.hi:
मेरी सबसे छोटी गति की छाप
रेशमी निस्तब्धता में दिखाई देती रहती है;
passages.bn:
আমার ক্ষুদ্রতম নড়াচড়ার ছাপ
রেশমি নীরবতায় দৃশ্যমান থাকে;
passages.id:
Jejak gerakanku yang terkecil
tetap tampak dalam keheningan selembut sutra;
passages.tr:
En küçük hareketimin izi
ipeksi sessizlikte görünür kalır;
passages.vi:
Dấu in từ chuyển động nhỏ nhất của tôi
vẫn hiện rõ trong tĩnh lặng mềm như lụa;
passages.th:
